mission.title: Healthcare matters too much to be locked inside a closed product.
mission.p1: Arab patients move between pharmacy, clinic and lab with no single connected record. Facilities are stuck between paper, closed local systems and foreign platforms that don't understand their context.
mission.p2: So we started Balsm as shared infrastructure: open code, open standards and open governance — built to outlast any single company.

privacyMeta.title: Privacy policy — Balsm
privacyMeta.description: What the balsm.health website collects, why, who handles it, and how to have it corrected or deleted. No health data, no trackers, no selling.

hero.title: Your data stays yours.
hero.subtitle: What this website collects, why, who handles it, and how to have it removed. Written plainly, so nothing that matters is hidden in legal language.

sections.title: What this policy covers
paragraphs: This policy covers the balsm.health website, in Arabic and English: its pages, its sign-up forms and the contributor frame tool.
It does not cover the Balsm apps or Balsm Cloud. Each will publish its own policy before it collects any data. This website collects no health or medical information of any kind.

sections.title: What we collect
paragraphs: We only collect what you type into one of our sign-up forms:

items.text: on the home, Cloud and providers pages: your email address, the language you were reading the site in, and which form you used.
if you fill them in: your organisation's name and your message.

sections.after: That is all. We don't ask for your name, your phone number or an account.

items.text: No analytics, advertising or social-media trackers.
No session recording. Error reports never include what you typed into a form.
Your photo in the contributor frame tool never leaves your browser. The frame is composed and downloaded on your device, and nothing is uploaded.

sections.title: How we use it
paragraphs: We use your email address to tell you about the launch or progress you signed up for, and, on the providers form, to reply to you. We use the language you were reading in to write to you in that language.

We process this data on the basis of your consent, which you give by submitting the form. You can withdraw it at any time. We never sell your data, and we never share it with anyone for their marketing.

sections.title: Who handles it for us
paragraphs: We rely on a small number of service providers, each handling only what its job needs:

items.text: stores the sign-up form submissions in our database.
hosts the website. Like any host, it processes each request, including your IP address, to deliver the page and protect it from abuse.
receives error reports so we can fix what breaks. It is configured to exclude your IP address, cookies and form contents, and email addresses are removed before a report is sent.
serves the site's typefaces. Your browser fetches them from Google's servers, which receive your IP address and browser details as part of that request.

sections.after: Some of these providers may process data on servers outside Egypt, under their own data-protection terms.

sections.title: Cookies and your browser
paragraphs: We don't set cookies. Cloudflare may set a strictly necessary security cookie to tell people from bots.
The links page remembers whether you chose the light or dark theme, in your browser's local storage. That setting never leaves your device, and clearing your browser data removes it.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: We keep a sign-up until you ask us to delete it, or until we no longer need it for the purpose you signed up for, whichever comes first. Sentry deletes error reports automatically after its retention period.

sections.title: How we protect it
paragraphs: Everything travels over HTTPS. The public side of the website can add a sign-up but cannot read the list back, and access to the list is limited to the Balsm team members who need it.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 151 of 2020), and similar laws where you live, you can ask to see the data we hold about you, correct it, delete it, or withdraw your consent.

To do any of these, email us from the address you signed up with, and we will act on it within 30 days. You can also correct your details at any time by submitting the same form again with the same email address.
If you believe we have mishandled your data, you have the right to complain to Egypt's Personal Data Protection Center.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: This website is not aimed at children, and we don't knowingly collect data from anyone under 18. If you believe a child has signed up, email us and we will delete it.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If what we collect or how we use it changes, we will update this page and the date at the top before the change takes effect.

contact.title: Questions or requests
contact.body: Write to us about anything on this page, or to access, correct or delete your data.

termsMeta.title: Terms and conditions — Balsm
termsMeta.description: The terms for using Balsm — the website, the Balsm app, Balsm Pro and Balsm Cloud. Not medical advice, adults only, your information stays yours.

hero.title: What we promise, and what we ask.
hero.subtitle: The terms for using Balsm: the website, the Balsm app, Balsm Pro and Balsm Cloud. Written plainly, with the most important parts first.

sections.title: About these terms
paragraphs: These terms apply to all of Balsm: the balsm.health website, the Balsm app, Balsm Pro and Balsm Cloud (together, “the services”). By using the services you agree to these terms and to our privacy policy. If you don't agree, please don't use them.
Balsm is an open-source healthcare technology project based in Egypt. In these terms, “Balsm”, “we” and “us” mean the Balsm team that runs the services.

sections.title: Not medical advice, and not an emergency service

items.text: Balsm helps you organise your health information. It does not diagnose, treat or give medical advice, and it doesn't replace a doctor, pharmacist or other qualified professional.

Always follow your healthcare provider's instructions about your medications and care. Reminders in the app are an aid, not a guarantee: a notification can be delayed or missed if your device is off, silenced or has notifications turned off.
In an emergency, call your local emergency number straight away: 123 in Egypt, 997 in Saudi Arabia, 998 in the UAE.

sections.title: Who can use Balsm
paragraphs: You must be 18 or older to create an account. Features that let parents or guardians manage a family member's health will come with their own terms.

If you use Balsm Pro for a clinic, pharmacy or other organisation, you confirm you are authorised to do so. That organisation is responsible for how it uses Balsm Pro and for the patient records it keeps, including meeting the healthcare and data-protection laws that apply to it.

sections.title: Your account
paragraphs: Keep access to your email, Google or Apple account secure, because it is how you sign in to Balsm. You are responsible for what happens under your account. If you think someone else has accessed it, sign out your other devices from the app and tell us straight away.

items.text: You own the information you add to Balsm. You give us only the permissions we need to store it, sync it and show it back to you, as described in our privacy policy.

You are responsible for keeping it accurate. Add information about other people, such as emergency contacts or members of your care team, only when you have a good reason to, and with their permission where it is needed.
When you share an emergency card, anyone with the link or QR code can read it until it expires or you revoke it. Share it only with people, and in places, you trust.

sections.title: Acceptable use
paragraphs: When you use Balsm, don't:

items.text: break the law, or use Balsm to harm anyone;
access, or try to access, another person's account or data;
overload, disrupt or try to break the security of our services, except through responsible disclosure to security@balsm.health;
upload malicious code, or create accounts by automated means;
pretend to be a healthcare provider, or anyone else, when you are not.

sections.title: Open source
paragraphs: Balsm's source code is published under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 with additional terms. Your rights to use, copy, change and share the code come from that licence, not from these terms, which cover your use of the services we run.
The licence doesn't let you rebrand Balsm or present it as your own, and it doesn't give you the right to use the Balsm name or logo in a way that suggests you are us or that we endorse you.

sections.title: Other companies' services
paragraphs: Some features rely on services from other companies, such as signing in with Google or Apple, or backing up to Google Drive or iCloud. Their own terms apply when you use them. Links to other websites are provided for convenience, and we are not responsible for their content.

sections.title: Availability and changes to the services
paragraphs: Some of the services are still in development, and we will keep improving them. We may add, change or remove features, and we will give you notice before a change that significantly affects you. Paid plans, such as parts of Balsm Cloud, will have their own terms that you will see and accept before you pay.

sections.title: Disclaimers
paragraphs: We work hard to keep Balsm reliable and accurate, but the services are provided “as is” and “as available”. To the extent the law allows, we don't promise that they will be uninterrupted, free of errors, or suitable for a particular purpose. Keep your own backup of information that matters to you.

sections.title: Limits on our liability
paragraphs: To the extent the law allows, Balsm is not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for decisions about your health made on the basis of information in the services.

Nothing in these terms limits liability that the law does not allow to be limited, such as liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud, and nothing in them takes away your rights as a consumer under the law where you live.

sections.title: Ending your use
paragraphs: You can stop using Balsm and delete your account at any time; our privacy policy explains what happens to your data. We may suspend or close an account that seriously or repeatedly breaks these terms, and we will tell you why unless the law prevents us.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: If we change these terms, we will update this page and the date at the top. For significant changes, we will tell you in the app before they take effect. If you keep using Balsm after that, you accept the updated terms.

sections.title: Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of Egypt, and disputes will be heard by the competent courts in Cairo. If you live in another country, you keep the protections the law there gives you as a consumer.

productsMeta.title: Balsm products — many products, one open core
productsMeta.description: Every Balsm product works on its own and connects to the rest over FHIR R4 — from the patient's pocket to the hospital lab.

hero.title: An open ecosystem, not a closed product.
hero.subtitle: An open core anyone can run, standards every system understands, and a community building on top — that is the Balsm ecosystem.

architecture.title: Your system inside your facility; cloud connection is your call.
architecture.desc: Balsm runs on a private server inside your facility, even without an internet connection. When needed, you can turn on the cloud connection to sync branches, while patient data stays inside the facility.

tiers.name: Devices
tiers.desc: Balsm apps on phone, tablet, web and desktop, from one codebase.

tiers.name: Facility server
tiers.desc: One workspace per server, hosted inside the facility, which fully owns its data.

tiers.name: Balsm Network
tiers.desc: An optional cloud layer for branch sync, backups and integrations.

standards.title: Built on open standards, from the first line.
standards.desc: No proprietary formats, no lock-in. What's written in Balsm can be read by any system that speaks FHIR.

licensing.title: Open forever. Sustainable by design.
licensing.desc: Balsm staying open source is non-negotiable. The managed cloud is what funds maintenance of the shared core.

selfHosted.title: Self-hosted
selfHosted.desc: Completely free. Run Balsm on your servers, modify it, and share your improvements with the community.

cloud.title: Managed cloud
cloud.desc: A Balsm Network subscription under the Balsm Commercial License — we run, update and back up; you focus on care.

newWs.title: Create a workspace
newWs.lead: A workspace is the container that brings your team and organizations together in one place. Once it exists, add whatever you need: a software company, hospitals, clinics, pharmacies and labs.
newWs.rolesLine: Members with roles: owner, admin, member
newWs.b1: One personal account can join several workspaces.
newWs.b2: Invite your team once; they work across every organization in the workspace.
newWs.b3: Pick the organization you act as from the menu at the top.
newWs.noteCare: Care recipient? You don't need a workspace.
newWs.noteInvite: Your organization already has a workspace? Ask its admin to invite you; the invite will appear in “My account”.
newWs.nameHint: A name your team recognizes; you can change it later.
newWs.handleHint: 3–30 characters: lowercase letters, digits, - or _. Link:
newWs.orgOk: I'm creating this workspace on behalf of an organization (a company or healthcare facility), not for personal use.
newWs.errOrgOk: Workspaces are for organizations only. Confirm you're creating it on behalf of a company or healthcare facility.
newWs.errHandle: Choose a handle for the workspace.
newWs.hShort: Handle is too short: at least 3 characters.
newWs.hChars: Use only lowercase Latin letters, numbers, - or _, and start with a letter.
newWs.hDash: Don't end with - or _, or repeat them back to back.

legal.title: Verify “{name}”
legal.lead: You can list your systems now and verify later. Once we review your documents, a “Verified” badge appears next to your company name and on all its systems — what health facilities look for before reaching out.
legal.ben1: A “Verified” badge on the company and its systems

legal.docBad: That file can't be used: a PDF or image, up to 10 MB.
legal.confirm: I confirm these documents are accurate, belong to this company, and that I'm authorized to submit them.
